title: What Happens If A Bullet Ant Stings You?

lines.text: This tiny insect delivers the most agonizing sting known to modern science.
Meet the South American bullet ant, named because its sting genuinely feels like being shot by a gun.
On the Schmidt sting pain index, it scores a four-plus: the absolute maximum level of pain.
When it stings, it clamps down with razor mandibles and injects a paralyzing neurotoxin called poneratoxin.
Poneratoxin targets your neurons, physically jamming your voltage-gated sodium channels permanently open.
This forces your pain receptors to fire non-stop electrical screaming signals into your spinal cord.
Within minutes, your heart races, cold sweats break out, and your entire limb shakes with violent, uncontrollable tremors.
Unlike a bee sting, this excruciating agony does not fade for twenty-four uninterrupted hours.
Yet the Sateré-Mawé tribe endures eighty stings in gloves to become warriors. Subscribe to Behind The Science for daily facts.
